shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large upright tan stone slab
horizontal band/register dividing the upper part of the surface from the figural scene below
row of repeated motifs along the top edge
animals/creatures rendered in profile with outstretched limbs
bird-like head with prominent beak in profile
small subordinate figure placed beside a larger one
curved, tapering appendages (wings/tails/plumes) filling the lower field
justification: Both are weathered upright stone slabs bearing shallow, flat-topped relief organised in the same broad scheme: a row of repeated motifs across the top, a narrow horizontal band of linear/zigzag ornament beneath it, and a larger figural field below in which profile creatures with beaked heads and small accompanying figures face one another. The clearest difference is in the vocabulary and density of the lower field — A is crowded with interlocking curvilinear scrolls, plumed headdresses and frontal-bodied anthropomorphs, while B keeps isolated, sparsely spaced animal silhouettes against blank stone, and the two slabs differ in outline (rounded-top stela versus a broad-headed T-shaped pillar).
